To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose an algorithm for provisioning resources in a multi-cloud environment, which takes into account the cost of SLA violations and the cost of database transitions to new cloud configurations; (2) we show that our algorithm is superior to the traditional approach, which aims to minimize the number of SLA violations, in that it minimizes the total cost of an application deployment; and (3) we demonstrate that our algorithm avoids the problem of thrashing of resources.

(1) the cost of a database deployment is the result of a complex interplay of the SLAs of the public and private cloud, (2) the cost of the database is a function of the number of SLA violations, (3) the cost of database deployment depends on the number of transitions between database configurations and (4) the number of database transitions is a function of SLA violations.

a cloud application’s QoS can be maintained while reducing its overall cost by using a look-ahead optimization algorithm that takes into account the SLAs furnished by the CSPs.
the cost of cloud applications can be significantly reduced by exploiting the flexibility of the underlying NoSQL-databases.
